facts.raw_span: 2-year history of gradual-onset right facial weakness leading to paralysis
denied hearing loss, tinnitus, imbalance, or other cranial nerve deficits
complete right facial paralysis
nonpulsatile mass protruding through the inferior ear canal
mild sensorineural loss at 4000 Hz
5 × 10-mm irregular lesion in the right mastoid near the stylomastoid foramen
heterogeneous enhancement on T1 with contrast
expansion of the fallopian canal distal to the second genu of the facial nerve
erosion of the posterior external auditory canal
expansion of the stylomastoid foramen
Pleomorphic hyperchromatic nuclei, staining positive for S100 and negative for KI-67
Low cellularity and low MIB-1 proliferation index

concepts.why: The patient's gradual-onset right facial weakness, nonpulsatile mass protruding through the inferior ear canal, and imaging findings of a lesion in the right mastoid near the stylomastoid foramen with heterogeneous enhancement on T1 with contrast are consistent with a facial nerve schwannoma.

The patient's nonpulsatile mass protruding through the inferior ear canal, imaging findings of a lesion in the right mastoid near the stylomastoid foramen, and pathology findings of a cartilaginous tumor with pleomorphic hyperchromatic nuclei are consistent with a chondrosarcoma.

rationales.F01: Gradual-onset facial weakness is consistent with a slow-growing tumor like facial nerve schwannoma.
rationales.F04: A nonpulsatile mass protruding through the inferior ear canal is highly suggestive of a tumor, and facial nerve schwannoma is a strong candidate.
rationales.F06: The location and appearance of the lesion on MRI are consistent with facial nerve schwannoma.
rationales.F11: Pleomorphic hyperchromatic nuclei staining positive for S100 are characteristic of schwannomas.
